speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning given your history; could you describe the specific area of the right arm where the weakness and numbness are most prominent? Additionally, do you notice any visible muscle wasting or atrophy in that limb?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy (Neurogenic Tumor/Neurolymphomatosis).

The combination of progressive focal weakness, sensory loss, burning pain, significant weight loss, and your history of anabolic steroid use strongly suggests a malignant nerve sheath tumor or lymphomatous infiltration of the brachial plexus. I am requesting an MRI of the right brachial plexus and a biopsy.
